title: Concept of equation
summary: Interpret an equation as a balance, test proposed solutions and recognise transformations that preserve the solution set.
objectives: Explain what it means for two expressions to be equal.
Test whether a value satisfies an equation by substitution.
Recognise that applying the same valid operation to both sides preserves equality.

blocks.text: An equation states that two expressions have the same value. A variable represents a number, and a solution is a value that makes the equation true. The equals sign describes a relationship between both sides; it does not mean that a calculation must always follow it.
When x = 4, the left side is 2(4) + 3 = 11, exactly matching the right side. The level balance in the diagram is a useful model: changing only one pan destroys the equality.

Equivalent equations have the same solution set. Equality is preserved when the same number is added to or subtracted from both sides, or when both sides are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero number. These actions undo operations while keeping the balance.

The double arrow means each equation is equivalent to the one before it. Dividing by zero is never valid. At this level, use operations whose inverse is defined and write each new equation on its own line so every change can be checked.

An expression such as 3x - 5 has a value but makes no claim of equality. An equation such as 3x - 5 = 10 can be true for some values and false for others. To test a proposed solution, substitute it into the original equation and evaluate the left and right sides separately.

A statement such as 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2 is true for every value because both sides simplify to the same expression. A statement such as x + 4 = x + 7 is never true because subtracting x would give 4 = 7. Recognising these cases prevents the false conclusion that every equation has exactly one solution.

sections.title: Worked example: test and transform an equation

prompt.text: Show that x = 5 satisfies 3x - 4 = 11, then write an equivalent equation after adding 4 to both sides.

content.text: Substitute x = 5 into the left-hand side.
The left side equals the right side, so x = 5 satisfies the equation.
Add 4 to both sides and simplify.

sections.verification_note: Substitution gives 11 = 11, and both 3x - 4 = 11 and 3x = 15 have the same solution x = 5.

sections.title: Worked example: choose a solution from candidates

prompt.text: Which of x = -2, x = 1 and x = 4 satisfies 2x + 5 = 3x + 1?

content.text: Rearrange the equation by subtracting 2x from both sides.
Check the matching candidate in the original equation.

sections.verification_note: Both sides equal 13 for x = 4. The other candidates fail substitution, so 4 is the only listed solution.

prompt.text: For 4x + 1 = 21, what value does the left-hand side have when x = 5?

feedback.text: Substituting x = 5 gives 4(5) + 1 = 21, matching the right-hand side.

blocks.text: Read the equals sign as a claim that two expressions have the same value. Test a proposed solution in the original equation by calculating both sides.
Keep an equation balanced by applying the same valid operation to both sides. Equivalent equations preserve the solution set; division by zero is never allowed.
